name: agent-question
purpose: A question the agent asks the reader in the middle of a run, before it can go on (a human-in-the-loop interrupt, Cloudscape follow-up input, the "ask the user" step of coding agents): pick one of a few options, type a short answer, or say yes or no. The card states the question, says why the agent asks, shows the answer control the question needs (`type`: options as radios, a one-line text field, or Yes and No buttons), and offers Submit and, when the run can go on without an answer, Skip. While the answer is sent the controls are inert and Submit shows its loading state; once answered, the controls give way to the answer in text (`Answered: Staging`) so the exchange stays in the thread; a failed send keeps the controls and shows the error line under them. It differs from `tool-approval`, which approves or denies a tool call with consequences: this card collects information the agent needs, and nothing runs on the reader's behalf. It also says "answer in flight" with `status="running"` instead of tool-approval's `loading` boolean, on purpose: the pause it renders already has a lifecycle (TanStack AI's `pending`, `validating` / `submitting`, `error`), and one `status` maps onto it without a second flag that could disagree with it. A block maps the interrupt like this: `pending` → `pending`; `validating`, `staged` and `submitting` → `running`; `error` → `error`, with the first of `errors[]` as `error`; a resolved interrupt → `success`; `cancel()` after Skip → `skipped`; an interrupt the run dropped → `canceled`. It is a card in the conversation, not a dialog: it does not trap focus and does not take initial focus; `focus()` moves focus to its heading when the owner wants to bring the reader to it.
useWhen: Use AgentQuestion only inside an AI conversation, when the agent pauses a run to ask the reader for information it cannot infer (a TanStack AI generic interrupt, an "ask the user" tool).
A choice between two to six named options: which environment, which plan, which of two fixes (`type="choice"`).
A short free-text answer: a name, a domain, a value the agent is missing (`type="text"`).
A yes-or-no question where both answers let the run go on (`type="confirm"`).
avoidWhen: The agent asks permission to run a tool or command with consequences → `tool-approval`.
Follow-up prompts the reader may send or ignore, with no paused run → `suggestion-group`.
A destructive action the reader started in the UI → `confirm-dialog`.
A form with several fields → `schema-form` in the page, not a chat card.
related: `tool-approval` — approve or deny an agent's tool call; same card language, different decision.
`suggestion-group` — optional follow-ups that start a new message instead of answering a paused run.
`chat-message` — the card sits in the assistant message; the assistant goes on in the next one.
`radio-group`, `input`, `button`, `status-indicator` — the parts the card is built from.
bestPractices: Ask one thing per card, as a question that ends with a question mark; put names and values in backticks (code).
Keep options short and mutually exclusive; give an option a `description` only when the label alone does not say what happens.
Offer Skip (`skippable`) only when the agent can continue without the answer, and have it say what it assumed.
Name the submit action after the outcome when it is not a generic answer (`Use this domain`).
Do not leave a question pending forever: when the run no longer needs it, set `status="canceled"`.
Offer at most six options; more than that is a search or a form, not a question.

props.name: title
props.doc: The question the agent asks, ending with a question mark. Backticks render as code.

props.name: description
props.doc: One or two sentences on why the agent asks or what it does with the answer; backticks render as code.

props.name: type
props.doc: The answer control: `choice` lists `options` as radios, `text` shows a one-line field, `confirm` shows No and Yes buttons.

props.name: options
props.doc: The answers of a `choice` question: `{ value, label, description?, disabled? }`. Ignored by the other types.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Short example shown in the empty field of a `text` question.

props.name: status
props.doc: `pending` asks; `running` sends the answer; `success`, `skipped` and `canceled` replace the controls with the outcome; `error` asks again.

props.name: error
props.doc: Why the last answer was not accepted, shown under the controls. Empty with `status="error"` uses the locale catalog.

props.name: skippable
props.doc: Offers Skip, for a question the agent can go on without.

props.name: submitLabel
props.doc: Text of the submit button (Yes on a `confirm` question). Empty uses the locale catalog (`Submit`, `Yes`).

props.name: declineLabel
props.doc: Text of the No button of a `confirm` question. Empty uses the locale catalog (`No`).

props.name: skipLabel
props.doc: Text of the Skip button. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Skip`).

slots.name: default
slots.notes: Context the reader needs to answer, between the question and the control: a `CodeBlock`, a `KeyValueList`.
